name: Naggai
overview: Naggai is a male figure mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus Christ, highlighting his role in the lineage of the Messiah as recorded in Luke 3:25. There is no tribal affiliation or additional notes provided about him. His inclusion underscores the historical and genealogical foundation of Christ's earthly ancestry.
namesAndTitles: The name Naggai appears once in Scripture without a given meaning or divine naming indication. It is simply presented as a proper name in Luke 3:25, without further elaboration on its significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Naggai as the son of Hesli, an inferred relationship from Luke 3:25, and the father of Maath, explicitly stated in Luke 3:26. These relationships place him within the direct ancestral line leading to Jesus Christ.
scriptureSignificance: Naggai's importance lies in his position within the Messianic genealogy, affirming the fulfillment of God's promise through a real historical lineage. His mention in Luke's genealogy connects the Old Testament heritage to the New Testament revelation in Christ, emphasizing God's sovereign plan through generations.
